title: Is Your Child Well Enough for School?
body:
Going to school regularly is important for learning, confidence, social development and wellbeing. If your child is unwell, it can sometimes be difficult to know whether they should attend.

As a general guide, children with **mild symptoms who are otherwise well, eating and drinking normally, and able to take part in learning** can usually attend school. If your child is too unwell to learn, needs to rest and recover, or has symptoms such as a **fever, vomiting or diarrhoea**, they should stay home.

For more information, please read the Ministry of Education’s guidance on knowing when a child is well enough to attend school, including common symptoms, when to stay home and when your child can return.

[Read the Ministry of Education guidance](https://www.education.govt.nz/news/how-decide-if-child-well-enough-be-school-or-early-learning)

If you are concerned about your child’s health, seek medical advice. **Healthline: 0800 611 116 (free, 24/7). In an emergency, call 111.**
excerpt: A quick guide for parents and caregivers on knowing when your child is well enough to attend school and when it is best to keep them home.
